title: Annotatio IV §.I cont.: Cosinus opens papal Transsubstantiation history with infallible Institution words
pass_a_gloss: Whence most rightly the Most Reverend Cosinus opens his History of papal Transsubstantiation with these words: The words brought forth by Christ the Lord in the solemn Institution of this most august sacrament for the perpetual memorial of Himself, namely, This is my body, which is given for you, This is my blood which is poured out for you, the whole holy Church throughout the world confesses to be altogether infallible and most true. But if anyone shall have affirmed the contrary, or dared to call Christ’s truthfulness into doubt, or derogated faith from His sayings, and not given his assent to them unless they are explained and twisted by a fiction and bare figure, him we neither can nor ought to tolerate or excuse in our Churches.
pass_b_english: Cosinus (Most Reverend) rightly opens his History of papal Transsubstantiation with the Institution words: This is my body given for you; This is my blood poured out for you — the whole Church confesses them infallible and most true.
Anyone who twists them into a fiction and bare figure, denying Christ’s truthfulness, we neither can nor ought to tolerate or excuse in our churches.
source_text: Unde rectissimè Reverendissimus Cosinus Historiam suam Transsubstantiationis papalis, his verbis auspicatur: Quæ à Christo Domino, in solenni hujus augustissimi sacramenti Institutione, ad perpetuam sui memoriationem, prolata sunt verba, nempe, Hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur, Hic est sanguis meus qui pro vobis effunditur, omnino infallibilia atque verissima esse, universa per orbem terrarum sancta confitetur Ecclesia. Si quis autem contrarium affirmaverit, aut veracitatem Christi in dubium vocare ausus fuerit, dictisve ejus fidem derogaverit, nec iis assensum suum præbuerit, nisi per figmentum & nudam figuram expositis & detortis, illum in Ecclesiis nostris nec tolerare, nec excusare vel possumus, vel debemus.
